BERT4Rec’s reconstruction/next-item mismatch is established: random interior masks permit future context, whereas appended-mask ranking uses history alone. [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) explicitly identifies weak alignment between item masking and sequential recommendation. Relevant 2024–2025 diagnostic work includes [Final-Model-Only Data Attribution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.03906): gradient methods approximate sensitivity to further training, with first-order accuracy sometimes high locally but deteriorating over longer updates. [Snapshot of Influence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19281) measures alignment between training-loss gradients and behavior-specific target gradients, although its experiments concern reinforcement learning, not BERT4Rec. Searches found no directly matching BERT4Rec ranking-boundary audit from 2024–2026.

A practical adaptation—not an established result—is to compute terminal-mask and reconstruction gradients on disjoint public training-prefix sets, matching supervised-target counts. For margin m = target score − tenth-highest negative score, measure −∇m·∇L by parameter block; positive values predict improvement under gradient descent. Report cosine alignment alongside magnitude, count tied embeddings once, and keep the boundary negative fixed for differentiation. Validate with reversible, equal-norm parameter perturbations in each objective’s descent direction; recompute candidate rankings afterward to capture boundary changes. Use dropout-free evaluation, several small perturbation sizes, and restore the checkpoint after every audit.

Compare these measurements with inexpensive history truncation, order-shuffling and masking ablations; test whether gradients explain additional differences on separate audit prefixes. Treat results as local sensitivity evidence, not causal retraining attribution or demonstrated recommendation improvement. Keep one trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category, charge audit computation to the search budget, and reserve improvement claims for unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
